content.text: Machine Learning is the subfield of computer science that gives computers the ability to perform tasks without being explicitly programmed. There are several different tasks that fall under the domain of machine learning and several different algorithms for "learning". Visualizing Classification

One interpretation of the classification task is that the model needs to learn how to use the input features to distinguish or separate the different classes as best it can. If we picture all of our datapoints as being points in some space, then ideally the datapoints belonging to one class would all cluster close to one another, but be distant from the datapoints belonging to other classes. The model's goal, then, is to learn where to draw one or more "lines", sometimes called decision boundaries, that neatly separate the points belonging to different classes. If the model can do that, it can make accurate predictions by predicting every point on one side of the line as belonging to one class, and every point on the other side of the line as belonging to another class.

(Aside: you may hear neural networks referred to as "nonlinear" models. Instead of only looking for straight lines to separate classes with, nonlinear models can also try separating classes by learning more complicated curves, which makes it possible to draw a boundary between datapoints not separable by any straight line. This is one reason why neural networks commonly outperform simpler models.)
